solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Closely examine small prison

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
can is slang for a prison or jail

explanation.surface: An inspector looks over a tiny jail cell by cell.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to look it over carefully, a direct synonym for scrutinise.

clue.text: Both Stuart and Dionne half-completed artist's workroom

indicators.note: only the first half of each name is finished off, so each of the two names gives just its opening three letters

explanation.surface: Two people, Stuart and Dionne, each left a job half done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both' is a link word telling you to treat each name the same way: Stuart gives STU and Dionne gives DIO.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is the room where a painter or sculptor works, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Trade show open

definitions.meaning: a trade ... is an exhibition where businesses show their goods
a ... contest is open and honest, above board

explanation.surface: An exhibition that is open to the public.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both an exhibition of goods and the adjective meaning just and above board.

clue.text: Jazz pianist favoured by royal relative after award

indicators.note: the favoured-royal-relative part comes after the award in the answer

parts.note: an Oscar is the Academy Award for film
a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword shorthand for royal or the Queen
a son is a relative

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist, a favourite of some royal relative, collects an award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal relative' looks like one person, but 'royal' gives ER and 'relative' gives SON separately; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a celebrated Canadian jazz pianist, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Unmarried man excited Chloe in pub

indicators.note: the stirred-up name is placed in the middle of the word for a pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

indicators.note: excited suggests the letters of the name are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: A single man gets a woman called Chloe worked up in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' makes the anagram; 'in' places it inside the pub word, which is split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a man who has never married, a straight synonym.

clue.text: One who stands against the old decaying gates enclosing unit

definitions.text: One who stands against the old

indicators.note: the rearranged gates wrap around the letter for unit, holding it inside
something decaying is falling apart, so the letters of gates crumble into a new order

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a unit

explanation.surface: Someone opposed to old things stands by rotting gates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decaying' signals the anagram and 'enclosing' puts the unit letter inside it; the definition is a cryptic-sounding description of a bigot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ageist discriminates against people because of their age, especially elderly people.

clue.text: Little Florence entertains blokes in Athletic club dance

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so the short name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Flo is a short form of the name Florence

indicators.note: the word for blokes sits inside the club's abbreviation

parts.note: men are blokes, British slang for chaps

explanation.surface: A girl called Flo hosts some men at a sports club dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: 'in' puts the blokes inside the club letters, and 'entertains' has the short name hold the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Spanish dance of Andalusia, an example of a dance.

clue.text: Sword nicked by girl

parts.note: nicked can mean cut slightly, as with a razor
a lass is a girl, especially in northern Britain

explanation.surface: A sword was stolen by a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nicked' reads as British slang for stolen, but here it means cut; 'by' just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword favoured by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Financial supporter not available to back hairdressing product

indicators.note: back tells you to read the abbreviation for not available backwards

parts.note: gel is used to style hair

explanation.surface: A backer is unavailable to fund a hair product launch.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is a private investor who backs a show or business venture, a specialised sense.

clue.text: Lowest emotional point of commemoration: a dirge

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters within the phrase, running across its words

explanation.surface: A mournful song at a memorial is the lowest point of grief.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'commemoratioN A DIRge'.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, here of one's spirits; in astronomy it is the point directly below.

clue.text: The aim's to change a lack of belief in god

definitions.text: a lack of belief in god

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are to be changed around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's aim is to convert another away from faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheism is disbelief in the existence of any deity, exactly what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Adult heard complaint raised

indicators.note: heard means the word for complaint is taken by its sound rather than spelling

parts.note: a groan is a complaint or moan
something raised is up

explanation.surface: An adult moans loudly about a complaint being brought up.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, the everyday informal word for one.

clue.text: US composer whinges awfully about intro of record

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the opening letter, surrounding it
awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled
the intro of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A composer complains bitterly about the start of a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns WHINGES into GESHWIN, which goes 'about' R.
explanation.definitionFit: George Gershwin was the American composer of Rhapsody in Blue, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Recalled article by North European on military general

indicators.note: recalled, called back, tells you to run the article and compass point backwards

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a Pole is a European from Poland

explanation.surface: An article recalled by a northern European writer about a general.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was the famous French general and emperor, a definition by example.

clue.text: Reveal temperature in Spanish city

indicators.note: the temperature letter goes in the middle of the city name

parts.note: Leon is a city in north-west Spain

explanation.surface: Someone discloses the temperature in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: To let on is to disclose a secret, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Again plan harvest around first of May

indicators.note: the word for harvest goes around the initial of the month

parts.note: to reap is to harvest a crop

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A farmer plans to bring in the crop around early May.
explanation.definitionFit: To remap is to chart or lay out a plan anew, the prefix supplying again.

clue.text: Perhaps calf is a beast of burden carrying sack regularly

indicators.note: the animal carries the picked letters inside it, as a load

parts.note: a mule is a beast of burden

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every other one starting from the first

explanation.surface: A young cow, perhaps, is a pack animal laden with a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calf' and 'beast of burden' suggest farm animals, but calf here is the leg muscle; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is a muscle at the back of the lower leg, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Violent storm forcibly split a party

parts.note: something torn has been ripped apart by force
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A violent storm tears a political party apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating windstorm, an example of a storm.

clue.text: Everyone outside potty over handsome young man

indicators.note: the word for everyone sits outside the potty, wrapping around it

parts.note: all means everyone
po is an informal word for a chamber pot or potty
O is the cricket scoresheet abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Everybody is crazy about a good-looking young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' reads as crazy but is the chamber pot, PO. An over is a set of six balls in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo, the beautiful Greek god, gives his name to any strikingly handsome young man.

clue.text: Swindler runs past new sleuth

indicators.note: the runs letter comes past, that is after, the rearranged word
new indicates the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A conman outruns a newly appointed detective.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a con artist who tricks people out of money, a synonym.

clue.text: A vocal expression in harmony

parts.note: tone of voice is a vocal expression

explanation.surface: A voice expressing itself in harmony with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To be at one with someone is to be in complete agreement, an idiom.

clue.text: First couple of children in A&E hurt

indicators.note: the opening letters are put in between the two letters of the hospital department

parts.note: A&E, accident and emergency, is the British hospital casualty department

indicators.note: the first couple of a word are its opening two letters

explanation.surface: The first two children arrive at casualty, injured.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is the emergency department of a British hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to hurt with a dull persistent pain, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: School prize went to son, finally

indicators.note: finally means take the final letter of each word in turn

explanation.surface: A prize was awarded to someone's son in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the famous English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is the well-known English public school, a definition by example.

clue.text: US soldier rejected toilet, dwelling in freezing conditions

indicators.note: rejected, thrown back, means the soldier's letters are turned backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
loo is British slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: An American soldier turned down a toilet in the icy cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dome house built from snow blocks, a home in the Arctic.

clue.text: Turned to welcome Shakespearean character

indicators.note: turned round, the short word is read backwards

parts.note: hello is a word of greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: Someone turned to greet a figure from Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is the Moorish general in Shakespeare's tragedy, a definition by example.
